docs.title: Bonus issues, stock splits and dividends: 10 stocks turning ex-record date this week. Do you own any?
docs.text:
Around 10 companies have scheduled record dates for bonus issues, stock splits and dividends during the week between October 5 (Monday) and October 9 (Friday).
 To be eligible for these corporate actions, investors must hold the shares in their demat accounts as of the respective record dates. The list is tentative, as more companies may announce record dates for dividends, bonus issues and stock splits during the week.
Also read | Why did market crash on Thursday? 
Here is the day-wise list of corporate actions to watch out for this week:
 October 5 (Monday) 
 Live Events
 NMDC has fixed Monday as the record date for its final dividend of Rs 1 per share. The PSU has declared 48 dividends since August 2002, and the stock has a dividend yield of 3.35%, according to data on Trendlyne.
The shares of the company have fallen around 8% in a week and 13% in a month, with the stock overall falling around 11% in 2026 so far. In the longer term, the shares of the company have delivered positive returns of more than 51% in three years and nearly 56% in five years.
 October 6 (Tuesday) 
 BLS E-Services has fixed Tuesday as the record date for its 1:2 stock split . This means that every share as on the record date will split into two shares following the stock split.
The value of each share will adjust to the corporate action on the record date.
 October 7 (Wednesday) 
 GTV Engineering has fixed Wednesday as the record date for a 2:1 bonus issue . This means that eligible shareholders will get two bonus shares for every one share held in the company as on the record date.
On the dividend side, PTC India will pay a dividend of Rs 5.5 per share to those shareholders who hold the stock on Wednesday.
 October 8 (Thursday) 
 Shankara Buildpro has fixed Thursday as the record date for its 1:5 stock split. This means that every share as on the record date will split into five shares following the stock split.
The value of each share will adjust to the corporate action on the record date.
Also read | Stocks to buy: Titan, Lenskart, Dabur among Nomura’s 17 consumer picks. Do you own any? 
 October 9 (Friday) 
 Mold-Tek Technologies and Mold-Tek Packaging both have fixed Friday as the record date for their respective 1:1 bonus issues. 
 DK Enterprises Global , Sahana System and Skyways Air Services meanwhile will turn ex-record date for their respective dividends, wrapping up the week.

docs.title: Semiconductor push, govt support driving EMS sector's growth, but valuation a concern: How 3 stocks with most buy calls are placed
docs.text:
Synopsis
 Investor enthusiasm around the sector is visible in the performance of nine EMS stocks covered by multiple brokerages. The group has delivered an equal weighted average return of 55.3% so far in 2026, compared with 1.1% for the Nifty 500 Equal Weighted Index. Seven of the nine stocks have delivered posi tive returns, while three have gained over 100%. The analysis is based on closing prices as of 28 September 2026.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 India’s electronic manufacturing services (EMS) sector is growing at a healthy pace, supported by rising demand for electronics and strong orders from sectors such as defence, aerospace, artificial intelligence (AI), automobiles, electric vehicles and clean energy. According to KPMG, one of the Big Four accounting firms, the Indian EMS industry has expanded from $10-12 billion in FY2019-20 to $40-45 billion in FY2024-25.
Yet, India accounts for just 5-6% of the global EMS market, leaving room for growth. The share is expected to rise over the coming decade, with KPMG projecting the Indian EMS industry to cross $150 billion by FY2029-30.
Growing export opportunities, the China-plus-one strategy, which involves companies diversifying their supply chains beyond China, and government support are some of the other key tailwinds. At the same time, domestic EMS companies are gradually moving beyond basic assembly to more complex, higher-value products, opening another avenue for growth. 
Investor enthusiasm around the sector is visible in the performance of nine EMS stocks covered by multiple brokerages. The group has delivered an equal-weighted average return of 55.3% so far in 2026, compared with 1.1% for the Nifty 500 Equal Weighted Index. Seven of the nine stocks have delivered positive returns, while three have gained over 100%. The analysis is based on closing prices as of 28 September 2026.
 Share of global EMS market in 2025 
Asia Pacific accounts for more than half of the global EMS market.
 Growth circuit 
 Government support
Government policies have played an important role in the sector’s growth. Initiatives such as Make in India and the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes have encouraged domestic manufacturing across segments including mobile phones, electronics, white goods, IT hardware and telecom equipment. The Electronic Component Manufacturing Scheme complements these initiatives by encouraging local production of critical components such as printed circuit boards, camera modules and display modules.
 Semiconductor push
The government’s semiconductor push could provide the next leg of growth for the electronics manufacturing ecosystem. While India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 1.0 focused on laying the foundation for semiconductor manufacturing, the recently approved ISM 2.0, or Semicon 2.0, aims to deepen the country’s semiconductor design and manufacturing capabilities. With a budgetary outlay of Rs.1.27 trillion, the programme will focus on semiconductor design, equipment, fabrication, advanced packaging, and research and development.
For EMS companies, greater availability of domestically manufactured semiconductors could strengthen supply chains, reduce dependence on imports and provide opportunities to move further up the value chain. Experts therefore see Semicon 2.0 as an important step in widening opportunities for Indian EMS players.
Raghavan Viswanathan, Partner, Deal Advisory, KPMG in India, says ISM 2.0 is aimed at long-term value creation and greater semiconductor self-reliance. “ISM 1.0 and 2.0, and possibly a future 3.0, could help make the 2030s India’s decade for semiconductors,” he says.
 Complexity, a growth driver
Another important shift is taking place within the EMS industry itself. As large original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) increasingly outsource manufacturing, domestic EMS companies are moving towards more complex applications. These require stronger engineering capabilities, certifications, testing, reliability and system-integration expertise.
A recent Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL) report argues that complexity, rather than scale alone, is becoming a key differentiator in the EMS business. As OEMs outsource more technically demanding products to specialised manufacturing partners, the addressable market for Indian EMS companies could expand. Greater complexity can also improve customer stickiness and provide EMS companies with a longer runway for growth.
Vinay Jain, Head of Research & Fund Manager at Karma Capital, remains positive on the long-term opportunity and believes the EMS story in India is changing. Companies are moving beyond simple assembly and printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) towards box builds, system integration, precision engineering and more complex electronics. In other words, the sector is gradually evolving from a capacity-led story to a capability-led one.
The shift towards higher-value products could also help margins. Analysts see scope for operating margin improvement as the product mix shifts toward areas such as automotive, industrial and defence electronics. Companies could also benefit from operating leverage as higher utilisation spreads fixed costs over a larger revenue base.
 Premium valuations
The sharp rally in EMS stocks, however, has also pushed valuations higher. According to Bloomberg data, the historical price-to-earnings ratios of the nine EMS companies range from 50 to 138 times. Five of the nine are trading at a premium of more than 20% to their respective five-year average valuations.
“Valuations are split, and investors should pay only for genuine depth of manufacturing,” says Manish Bhandari, CEO and Portfolio Manager, Vallum Capital.
Bhandari expects much of the benefit from ISM 2.0 to emerge between FY2026-27 and FY2028-29 and believes investors should build positions gradually. “This is a stock picker’s market: leadership will be concentrated in the few companies moving up the value chain, not spread acro

docs.title: France's Schneider Electric nears $20 billion deal to buy US software group PTC: Report
docs.text:
France's Schneider Electric is nearing a deal to buy US software group PTC for about $20 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday citing people with knowledge of the matter.
 A deal may be announced as soon as Monday, the newspaper said, adding that discussions between the two companies were ongoing and there was no certainty they would result in a deal.
Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. Schneider Electric and PTC did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment outside regular business hours. 
Boston-based PTC has a market value of $15.63 billion, according to LSEG data.
In July, the company had lifted its annual revenue forecast after third-quarter results, betting on strong demand for its core industrial software and artificial intelligence-powered tools.

docs.title: AceVector shares to list today; Check GMP ahead of debut
docs.text:
Shares of AceVector are set to debut on the BSE and NSE on Monday, October 5, with grey market sentiment remaining cautious ahead of the listing. The IPO currently commands a grey market premium (GMP) of 2%, indicating a modest premium over the issue price.
 The Rs 420-crore public issue was priced in the range of Rs 30–32 per share, with the upper end of the price band at Rs 32. The issue comprised a fresh issue of 8.97 crore shares aggregating to Rs 287 crore and an offer for sale (OFS) of 4.16 crore shares worth Rs 133 crore.
 Read more: Vishal Nirmiti IPO Day 3: GMP at 9%; Check subscription, key details and analyst view 
The IPO opened for subscription on September 25 and closed on September 29, 2026. The issue was subscribed 5.07 times overall. The retail portion was subscribed 4.83 times, while the qualified institutional buyers (QIB) category, excluding anchor investors, was subscribed 3.42 times. The non-institutional investors (NII) category saw subscription of 8.53 times by the final day.
The share allotment was finalised on September 30, with the company scheduled to list its shares on both the NSE and BSE on October 5, 2026.
 Live Events
The IPO had a lot size of 468 shares. At the upper price band of Rs 32 per share, retail investors required a minimum investment of Rs 14,976 for one lot.
 IIFL Capital Services Ltd. , CLSA India Pvt. Ltd. and Systematix Corporate Services Ltd. are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while MUFG Intime India Pvt. Ltd. is the registrar.
 AceVector IPO GMP Today
The AceVector IPO is commanding a grey market premium (GMP) of Rs 1 per share, or around 2% over the upper price band of Rs 32. Based on the prevailing GMP, the estimated listing price is Rs 33 per share. However, the grey market premium is an unofficial indicator of market sentiment and does not guarantee the actual listing price or returns.
 Read more: Orient Cables shares to list today; GMP signals 45% premium over issue price 
 IPO Proceeds
The company plans to utilise Rs 132 crore of the net IPO proceeds to fund a portion of the marketing and business promotion expenses of its Marketplace business. Another Rs 50 crore will be used towards technology infrastructure costs for the Marketplace business.
The remaining proceeds will be utilised for inorganic growth through acquisitions and general corporate purposes. The total amount earmarked under the specified IPO objects is Rs 182 crore.
 Financial Performance
 Acevector Ltd. ’s total income increased 32%, rising from Rs 407 crore in FY25 to Rs 538 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, the company narrowed its net loss significantly to Rs 45 crore in FY26, from Rs 126 crore in FY25.
 About Acevector Ltd.
Incorporated in 2007, Acevector Ltd. operates an asset-light digital commerce ecosystem through its subsidiaries, spanning data, technology, and AI-driven businesses. Its operations include a value-focused e-commerce marketplace, e-commerce enablement SaaS platforms, and consumer brand businesses.
The ecosystem comprises: (i) Snapdeal, a value-driven lifestyle e-commerce marketplace offering affordable and quality merchandise across lifestyle categories (ii) Uniware, Convertway, and Shipway, providing a comprehensive suite of e-commerce enablement SaaS products that support end-to-end e-commerce operations; and (iii) Stellaro Brands, an omnichannel portfolio of value-focused consumer brands. In FY 2026, Snapdeal served customers nation-wide across 18,972 pin codes in India, primarily catering to middle-income, value-conscious consumers in Tier 2+ and smaller cities—an important segment of the large untapped value e-commerce market.

docs.title: Will Nifty, Sensex plunge for 9th straight week? TCS Q2, 4 factors to drive Dalal Street from Monday
docs.text:
Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen
 Loading...

 Unlock AI Briefing and Premium Content

 The Indian stock market has just set a record, but not one investors hoped for. Dalal Street has logged losses for eight consecutive weeks for the first time in 25 years, surpassing the streaks seen during the 2020 Covid-19 crash and the 2008 global financial crisis.
 A confluence of rising oil prices, soaring bond yields, and inflation worries has dented sentiment on the bourses, triggering a major selloff in Indian equities.
 Here are 5 factors that could affect D-Street move in the coming week: 
 Oil prices 
For the week, oil prices were subdued after European leaders agreed to US President Donald Trump’s request to release diesel reserves in an effort to bring down fuel prices and reduce imports of the fuel from the United States.
 Live Events
But analysts remain on edge. "We simply don't know how to model the endgame," JPMorgan analysts said, highlighting the uncertainty over how the conflict could develop. When the conflict began, the bank had assumed there were economic thresholds the US administration would not cross. Six months into the war, JPMorgan said many of those thresholds had been crossed, while there was still no clear exit strategy.
The risk of further supply disruptions has also increased the possibility of higher oil prices. Daan Struyven, co-head of global commodities research at Goldman Sachs, said recent attacks had shown that disruptions to shipping could spread and become more severe. Goldman Sachs has outlined a scenario in which oil prices could rise as high as $120 a barrel if attacks on vessels in the Middle East intensify. If exports return to normal, the bank expects oil prices to move back towards $80 a barrel.
 RBI MPC meet 
The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) is scheduled to meet from October 5-7, to decide on the benchmark repo rate. Economists now expect the Central Bank to begin a rate-hiking cycle, bringing forward their earlier call for a December hike.
A 25 bps hike in October, rather than December as previously forecast, is possible amid higher energy prices, food inflation and wider price pressures which strengthen the case for tighter policy, according to Bank of America (BofA).
“After almost two years of monetary accommodation, the RBI appears set to take early steps to start withdrawing the policy support in October MPC. As such, we now believe that the RBI will go ahead with a rate hike of 25bp in October MPC,” said BofA.
The balance of risks has tilted decisively towards a 25-bps rate hike by the RBI at this juncture, as a combination of broadening inflationary pressures, worsening global macros, evolving liquidity conditions and a renewed global repricing of risks is making the case for pre-emptive action stronger, SBI Research said in its report.
 Bond yields 
The 10-year US Treasury yield, a yardstick for borrowing costs and asset prices globally, rose to 5.34%, its highest since 2002. A sharp rise in the 10-year US Treasury yield can pressure Indian stocks because it makes US government bonds more attractive relative to riskier emerging-market assets. Higher US yields can encourage global investors to move money out of markets such as India, putting pressure on the rupee and equities.
A weaker rupee can further raise imported costs, particularly for companies dependent on crude oil and other overseas inputs.
 FII selloff worsens 
FIIs have offloaded Rs 43,687 crore in just six trading sessions, with outflows accelerating over the past three sessions. Their index futures long-short ratio has declined to 8.01%, near the lower end of its historical range.
Foreign selling was understandable in the current global rate environment. In the context of the 10-year US bond yields hovering around 5.2%, this FII selling is a rational act, experts say.
Foreign investors are unlikely to return to Indian equities in large numbers even after the artificial intelligence trade peaks. A sustained revival in foreign inflows depends on India's ability to build globally competitive industries in areas such as semiconductors, batteries and energy storage, Bernstein said in a report.
 Q2 earnings 
TCS, DMart are among 21 companies which will declare its Q2 earnings to officially kickstart the earnings session. could provide important cues for market sentiment, particularly as investors look for signs of resilience in corporate earnings amid a volatile global backdrop. TCS results will be watched for revenue growth, deal wins, margins and management commentary on IT spending, while DMart's numbers will offer a read on consumer demand, sales growth and operating margins.
Any significant deviation from expectations in either set of results could influence sentiment not only towards the respective stocks but also across the broader IT and consumption segments.
 Rupee plunge 
The Indian rupee fell to a two-month low as a sharp rise in global bond yields to decade highs and higher oil prices added to pressure on the currency, which was already facing headwinds from foreign portfolio outflows.
Persistent pressure on the rupee has also kept exporters cautious about hedging their receivables, even as importer hedging remains strong. This has further widened the demand-supply mismatch in the foreign exchange market.
FX advisory firm IFA Global recommends that exporters hedge cautiously and only against in-hand orders, while importers should use dips in the dollar-rupee pair to hedge their exposure, Reuters reported.
 Technical outlook

While Motilal Oswal remains upbeat on Jindal Steel & Power and Gopal Snacks, citing strong growth visibility and margin improvement, Citi maintains a Sell on Hindustan Zinc despite supportive silver trends. Stock-specific fundamentals continue to shape differentiated outlooks.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

Equity benchmarks remained under selling pressure throughout last week, with the Nifty 50 falling 0.88 percent on October 1 amid weak market breadth. About 2,556 stocks declined, compared with 729 stocks that advanced on the NSE. The market may witness a rebound after entering oversold territory, but the sustainability of any recovery will be key to watch. Here are some short-term trading ideas to consider:
 Jay Mehta, Technical Research at JM Financial Services 
 Capillary Technologies India | CMP: Rs 554.7 
Capillary Technologies witnessed a strong rally in September, moving from around Rs 440 to Rs 608, and is now undergoing a retracement. The earlier upmove was supported by strong volumes, while the current pullback is taking place on relatively lower volumes, indicating that the overall setup remains positive.
The stock is trading near its short- and medium-term moving averages, while momentum and trend indicators remain bullish.
Cyient is consolidating in a tight range following a strong rally and subsequent retracement. The stock witnessed a strong breakout above the range on September 30, accompanied by significant volumes, indicating strong market participation.
It is currently trading above its short-, medium-, and long-term moving averages, while momentum and trend indicators remain supportive of a bullish bias.
 Star Health and Allied Insurance Company | CMP: Rs 537.7 
On the weekly chart, Star Health is currently retracing towards its previous breakout zone above the resistance trendline, which was broken in June 2026. The stock is trading above its long-term moving averages on the daily chart and around its 200-week moving average on the weekly chart, where it is finding support.
The broader structure remains positive, with higher highs and higher lows, while the latest candle indicates buying interest near key moving-average support.
 Jatin Gedia, Technical Research Analyst, VP, Derivatives & Technical Research at Teji Mandi 
JSW Infrastructure has been forming higher highs and higher lows on the daily chart, suggesting an uptrend. It tested the triangle-pattern breakout at Rs 341 and formed a long-legged bullish candle on the daily chart, suggesting strong buying interest.
The stock has held above the 20-day moving average and the 40-day moving average at Rs 345 and Rs 340, respectively, keeping the short-term uptrend intact.
The daily momentum indicator has given a positive crossover, which is a buy signal. Thus, both the price pattern and momentum setup suggest that the stock is poised for an upmove over the next few trading sessions.
Infosys has formed a double-bottom pattern in the Rs 1,000-980 zone. It formed a Hammer candlestick pattern and also witnessed follow-through buying interest, surpassing the previous six-day high and suggesting a short-term trend reversal.
The daily momentum indicator has triggered a fresh positive crossover along with a positive divergence, which is a buy signal. Thus, the bullish price pattern and momentum setup suggest that the stock could reverse the current downtrend and witness a short-term rally.
 Sun Pharmaceutical Industries Futures | CMP: Rs 1,816.40 
Sun Pharmaceutical has been forming lower highs and lower lows on the daily chart, suggesting a downtrend. Last week, it broke down after a two-week consolidation, suggesting the resumption of the next leg of the decline. It also closed below the 200-day moving average at Rs 1,823, suggesting weakness.
The daily momentum indicator has triggered a negative crossover, which is a sell signal. Thus, considering the fresh breakdown and the bearish crossover on the momentum indicator, further weakness could be expected.
 Hitesh Tailor, Technical Research Analyst at Choice Broking 
 Schneider Electric Infrastructure | CMP: Rs 1,275.4 
Schneider Electric Infrastructure is currently exhibiting strong bullish momentum after a period of consolidation, with the stock closing around Rs 1,275. The price has delivered a clear breakout from a sideways range and successfully crossed and closed above its 50-day EMA near Rs 1,242.40, confirming a renewed short-term uptrend.
The weekly and daily structures indicate that the stock has established a firm base along the 50-day and 200-day EMAs near Rs 1,188.90-1,125.30. The RSI has taken solid support around its midpoint zone at 47.85 and bounced strongly upwards to 57.42, signalling expanding buying momentum with significant upside room remaining.

docs.title: Stock recommendations for 5 October from MarketSmith India
docs.text:
Markets 
 Stock recommendations for 5 October from MarketSmith India
 MarketSmith India 12 min read 5 Oct 2026, 06:01 AM IST 
 Summary
 MarketSmith India reveals its top stock recommendations for today, 5 October. Get expert insights into the best-performing stocks to guide your investment decisions. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Stock market recap: Indian equities fell for a fourth straight session on Thursday, while the market posted its eighth consecutive weekly loss, its longest such losing streak since 2001.
 The Nifty 50 fell 198.50 points, or 0.88%, to close at 22,421.95, its lowest level since April, after hitting an intraday low of 22,217.30. The Sensex lost 570.59 points, or 0.79%, to settle at 71,909.70. The Nifty fell about 3.1% during the holiday-shortened week.
 A rebound in crude oil prices, higher US bond yields and a rupee that weakened past 96 to the dollar added to the pressure.
 Auto stocks were hit hardest after weak September sales, with Bajaj Auto falling about 8%. Maruti, M&M, and Eicher Motors also declined. Hospital stocks, including Apollo Hospitals and Max Healthcare, extended losses amid concerns over drug-price controls. Metals and FMCG stocks were also weak.
 IT stocks and Kotak Mahindra Bank provided some support. Kotak Mahindra Bank rose about 3% after naming a new chief executive.
 Market breadth was negative, with 1,023 stocks advancing, 2,574 declining and 110 unchanged. Indian stock markets will remain shut on Friday, and the Reserve Bank of India’s policy decision is the next key event markets will wait for.
 Two stock recommendations by MarketSmith India: 
 Buy: GNG Electronics Ltd (current price: ₹ 705) 
 Why it’s recommended: India’s largest organized refurbished ICT device player, benefiting from rising demand for affordable and sustainable laptops/desktops along with strong global presence across multiple countries. An integrated sourcing-refurbishment-distribution model, expanding enterprise partnerships, and increasing acceptance of refurbished devices support scalable revenue growth and margin expansion. 
 Key metrics: P/E: 54.97, 52-week high: ₹ 730.00, volume: ₹ 61.47 crore 
 Technical analysis: Trendline Breakout 
 Risk factors: Business is highly dependent on the availability of used IT assets and procurement relationships; any disruption in sourcing can impact volumes and profitability. Intense competition from new-device manufacturers and other refurbishers, along with technology obsolescence, could pressure margins and demand. 
 Buy: ₹ 698–709 
 Target price: ₹ 820 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 666 
 Buy: Paisalo Digital Ltd (current price: ₹ 80) 
 Why it’s recommended: Strong co-lending partnerships with banks and a technology-driven lending platform enable rapid AUM growth while expanding financial inclusion in underserved rural and semi-urban markets. Large customer base, improving geographic reach, and scalable business correspondent model provide a long runway for credit growth.
 Key metrics: P/E: 27.72, 52-week high: ₹ 94.88, volume: ₹ 123.23 crore 
 Technical analysis: Bounce back from its 50-DMA 
 Risk factors: Exposure to economically vulnerable borrowers makes asset quality sensitive to rural income stress, economic slowdowns, and challenges of collection. Regulatory changes affecting NBFCs, co-lending frameworks, interest rates, or digital lending practices could impact growth and profitability. 
 Buy at: ₹ 79–80 
 Target price: ₹ 90 in two to three months 
 Stop loss: ₹ 76 
 How Nifty 50 performed 
 On 1 October, Indian equities ended sharply lower, although a late-session recovery helped the benchmark indices close well above their intraday lows. The Nifty 50 fell 198.50 points, or 0.88%, to 22,421.95 after hitting an intraday low of 22,217.30, while the Sensex ended around 71,910, down about 570 points.
 Market breadth remained distinctly weak. Exchange-wide data at 4 pm showed 1,023 stocks advancing, against 2,574 declining and 110 unchanged. This translates to an advance-decline ratio of roughly 0.40, pointing to broad-based selling beyond the headline indices.
 On the sectoral front, IT was the clearest outperformer, rising 2.17%, while private banks were broadly flat. Auto (-3.46%), Metal (-2.35%), Media (-2.33%), Consumer Durables (-1.91%) and FMCG (-1.61%) led the declines. Persistent foreign institutional selling, elevated US bond yields and volatility in crude oil prices weighed on sentiment.
 The Nifty 50 remains firmly in a bearish price structure, extending its sequence of lower highs and lower lows. The index has decisively broken below the horizontal consolidation structure visible on the daily chart and continues to trade below all major moving averages, reinforcing the prevailing downtrend. The earlier rising trendline has also been breached, with subsequent price action failing to reclaim it, pointing to a deterioration in the medium-term trend.
 Momentum indicators remain weak. The RSI has fallen to around 22.6, deep in oversold territory and below its signal average, highlighting intense negative momentum. This raises the possibility of a short-term mean-reversion move, but does not by itself confirm a trend reversal. The MACD remains below both its signal line and the zero line, while the negative histogram persists, confirming that bearish momentum remains dominant.
 The Nifty 50 registered a fresh low near 22,200 before recovering part of its intraday losses. On the downside, 22,200–22,000 remains a key support zone. A sustained break below this band could intensify selling pressure and potentially extend the decline towards 21,700–21,600. Conversely, any near-term recovery is likely to face initial resistance at 22,600–22,800, which has emerged as a key technical hurdle following the recent breakdown.
 How did the Nifty Bank perform? 
 Nifty Bank opened on a negative note at 54,583.

docs.title: Tata Comms, Siemens, Aadhar Housing, Styrenix, Sudarshan — Top 5 stocks to buy on Monday | Target, SL by Sumeet Bagadia
docs.text:
The Nifty 50 index finished at 22,421, logging a weekly loss for the eighth straight session, whereas the BSE Sensex fell nearly 2000 points. The Bank Nifty index finished at 54,450. All three key benchmark indices witnessed strong selling throughout the truncated week. Sumeet Bagadia, Executive Director at Choice Broking, believes the Indian stock market bias has further weakened as the Nifty 50 index approaches its near-term support at 22,200. Going down memory lane, Sumeet Bagadia said that, in 2008, the Nifty 50 declined for seven consecutive weeks before witnessing a five-week positive move. Speaking on the outlook for the Nifty 50 index, Sumeet Bagadia said, “The short-term structure continues to show weakness, with sustained selling pressure over the last eight weeks keeping the broader market under pressure. The index is currently holding around the 22,400 zone, but a sustained move above 22,600 would be important for a stronger recovery.” Bagadia said that PCR at 0.99 indicates a relatively balanced options setup, while the highest Call OI concentration is seen around 22,400–22,500 and the highest Put OI concentration around 22,400–22,300, making this zone important for the near-term price action. The Choice Broking expert said that if the 50-stock index closes above 22,600 for two consecutive sessions, a stronger pullback could be expected. Historically, in 2008, Nifty declined for seven consecutive weeks before witnessing a five-week positive move. Immediate support is seen at 22,100–22,200, while resistance is at 22,600/22,800. Regarding stocks to buy on Monday, Sumeet Bagadia recommended these top 5 breakout stocks: Siemens Energy India (ENRIN), Aadhar Housing Finance, Styrenix, Tata Communications, and Sudarshan Chemicals. The Siemens Energy India share has shown a fresh expansion in its daily price action after breaking out of its recent trading range and sustaining above the highs of the previous two sessions, with volume support. The stock has further strengthened its technical positioning by sustaining and closing above both the 21-Day and 200-Day EMAs, reflecting a supportive trend across short- and long-term timeframes. Momentum confirmation is also evident in the MACD, which has generated a positive crossover and indicates improving upside momentum. The breakout, therefore, carries support from price, volume and momentum indicators. With ₹ 3,180 as the key risk level, continued follow-through could keep the stock advancing towards the ₹ 3,660 target. Aadhar Housing Finance's share has shown a notable improvement in its daily price action after breaking above the highs of the previous three trading sessions, with rising volumes supporting the move and reflecting stronger participation. Prior to the breakout, the stock found demand near the major support zone of ₹ 430 to ₹ 433, with the lower Bollinger Band providing additional support. This support-based reversal has helped improve the short-term price structure. The stock has shown a positive shift in its daily price action after breaking out of a well-defined trading range, signalling renewed buying interest and a potential reversal in the prevailing trend. The breakout stock is currently trading around ₹ 1,683 and appears to be showing a potential bullish setup. The stock has broken out of a sideways consolidation range, supported by a volume-backed candle, indicating increased buying participation. A major support zone is observed near 1,640, which also aligns with the lower Bollinger Band, reinforcing the support. Additionally, the RSI shows bullish divergence, suggesting improving momentum and a possible reversal from recent weakness. Sudarshan Chemicals' share is showing improving price action on the daily chart after taking support near its rising trend line, with a volume-backed candlestick highlighting renewed buying participation from the support zone. The stock has further strengthened its short-term structure by sustaining above the 21-Day EMA, indicating that the recent recovery is gaining traction. Momentum is also turning favourable, as the RSI has rebounded from the 50 mark, suggesting a gradual shift towards positive momentum and improving buyer interest. docs.title: Top 5 IT stocks to buy today: TCS, Infosys, Mphasis, Coforge, Persistent Systems | Experts' view; Nifty FPI 150 heatmap
docs.text:
According to stock market experts, Indian IT companies receive more than 50% of their average business from the US, with Accenture playing a major role. After the better-than-expected Accenture results, the market expects similar Q2 results from the Indian IT giants. As the market has a track record of discounting events well before they take place, we can expect strong buying in Indian IT stocks on Monday. However, they suggested that short-term investors take a cue from the Nifty FPI heatmap. They said that of the 50 stocks in the Nifty FPI index, 20 ended in the green despite a heavy stock market crash on Thursday. Of those 20 stocks, 5 belong to the IT segment, suggesting foreign investors were betting heavily on these Indian IT stocks ahead of Accenture's results on Thursday. Decoding the Nifty FPI heatmap to get a higher return on one's money, Anuj Gupta, a SEBI-registered market expert, said, “Nifty FPI 150 Index heatmap signals about the top 50 Indian stocks, which is highly traded by the foreign investors. As FPIs are bullish on certain stocks, they are expected to attract DIIs as well. As the Accenture results is expected to attract DIIs on Monday, it would be important to know the IT stocks that are expected to outperform others. For this, they have two options: one is the Nifty FPI heatmap, and the other is Indian IT stocks listed on the NYSE.” The SEBI-registered expert said that of the 50 stocks in the Nifty FPI Index, 20finished in the green despite a heavy sell-off on Thursday. Of those 20 stocks, 5 are in the IT segment: Mphasis, Coforge, Infosys, TCS, and Persistent Systems . “As these stocks are in the bull trend ahead of the expected rally, an investor can expect a sharp upside in these 5 IT stocks when the market opens,” said Anuj Gupta. On why the Nifty FPI index is important in selecting an intraday stock, Anuj Gupta said, “Nifty India FPI 150 Index tracks the top 150 accessible and investible stocks from the Nifty 500 tailored for foreign portfolio investors.” On why Accenture results hold the key for the Indian IT companies, Mahesh M Ojha, VP — Research & Business Development at KC Securities, said, “Indian IT companies draw more than 50% of their business from the US. Accenture plays a big role in it. Some Indian IT companies draw more than 50% of their business from the US. So, we are bullish on those IT stocks that draw more than 50% of their business from the US.” Ojha said that shares of Sagility, Birlasoft, Mphasis, Persistent Systems, and LTIMindtree are expected to outperform other Indian IT stocks, as they derive more than 50% of their business from the US. Compared with the Nifty FPI heatmap, Mphasis and Persistent Systems have a higher probability of moving higher, as they are expected to receive favour from both FPIs and DIIs. docs.title: LTM, Cyient, Zen, Birlasoft share price target, stop-loss - IT stocks to buy for over 32% returns ahead of Q2 results
docs.text:
The brokerage has retained a positive stance on most of the IT stocks, with Larsen & Toubro Technology Services (LTTS), Mphasis and Coforge among the picks offering meaningful upside from current levels.
TCS has a new target price of ₹ 2,470, implying 20% upside, with an ‘ADD’ rating, while Infosys has a target of ₹ 1,250, offering 26% upside, and retains a ‘BUY’ rating, according to the firm.
 HCL Technologies has a revised target of ₹ 1,370, implying 11% upside, with an ‘ADD’ rating, while Wipro has a ₹ 185 target, indicating 17% upside. Tech Mahindra has a target of ₹ 1,660, offering 9% upside, with an ‘ADD’ rating. Among the larger opportunities, L&T Technology Services has a revised target of ₹ 5,270, implying 30% upside, and retains a 'BUY' rating.
Mphasis has a target of ₹ 2,840, offering 32% upside, while Persistent Systems has a target of ₹ 6,070, implying 15% upside; both has been assigned ‘ADD’ rating by the brokerage firm.
According to HDFC Securities Indian IT sector is expected to report weak growth in the second quarter of FY27, even though this period is usually considered a strong quarter for the industry.
Growth for large IT companies is estimated to range from a 0.4% decline to 2% growth sequentially, while mid-sized IT firms could see growth of 0.6% to 6.3%, partly helped by acquisitions, the firm said.
The firm further said that new business deals remain weak, while clients are taking longer to make decisions and continue to cut discretionary technology spending because of economic uncertainty. IT companies are also facing pricing pressure as clients increasingly expect them to pass on the cost savings from higher productivity through AI.
With the first half of FY27 likely to be weaker than expected, the sector's recovery now depends heavily on the second half. However, the third quarter is usually weaker because of seasonal factors such as employee furloughs. This could limit the overall growth outlook for FY27.
“Despite weak near-term growth, valuations have fallen close to historical lows and free cash flow yields remain attractive. The brokerage has therefore reduced its revenue estimates for FY27-FY29 by around 0.4-0.6%, lowered valuation multiples by 1-2 times for some stocks, and shifted its valuation base to September 2028 earnings,” it said.

These, along with the downward repricing of loan rates, have been a drag on NIMs. Like most large banks, HDFC Bank could benefit from any rate hikes, as c.70% of loans are linked to EBLR/floating rates, but recalibrating the risk profile toward higher-risk-adjusted segments such as SME/Business banking loans, gold loans, and unsecured personal loans could also support ROA expansion. Maintain Buy call with PT of ₹ 880 based on 1.6x Sep 2028E PB; ADR PT (Price Target) at $28.” So, the Jefferies India report has set a ₹ 880 price target for HDFC Bank in the Indian stock market and a $28 price target for the HDFC Bank ADR on the NYSE. Management aims to build Athiva into a leading pan-India premium hospitality brand (1,200-1,500 keys). Co targets higher leisure mix & selective market expansion, while its high-margin CRE portfolio provides recurring CFs that underpin growth & earnings stability.” The Jefferies India report further added that management's vision extends beyond adding room inventory, focusing instead on building a scaled owner-operator ecosystem through large-format asset ownership, selective geographic expansion, growth of its owned brand Athiva, & increased use of franchise-led models. Partnerships such as Marriott's Autograph Collection & IHCL's first Taj franchise with Chalet underscore its rising operating credibility, while stable annuity income from commercial RE provides the capital flexibility to fund future growth. The global brokerage said that management outlined its rapid growth plans, supported by its 2,036-key development pipeline (including recent additions in Pune & Hyderabad totalling ~380 keys). Growth is expected to be largely execution-led, with existing assets contributing half of the EBITDA growth over the next 5 years, driven by LFL growth and asset sweating and the other half through new projects/ acquisitions. Management expects RevPAR growth in mid-to-high single digits, supporting overall revenue growth in the mid-teens. The Chalet Hotels' management continues to expand beyond its traditional Western India concentration but remains disciplined in market selection. Recent additions in Aravali, the Himalayas & Udaipur, alongside the upcoming Taj property at Delhi Airport, reflect a conscious effort to build a stronger presence in Northern India. Near-term additions include the phased opening of Taj Delhi Airport (starting with ~70 rooms) and Athiva South Goa over the next 18-24 months, following approvals which are expected by Jan-27. docs.title: All B-1 bombers returning to US from UK base
docs.text:
Global 
 All B-1 bombers returning to US from UK base
 Shelby Holliday , Michael R. Gordon , Max Colchester , The Wall Street Journal 2 min read 5 Oct 2026, 06:15 AM IST 
 Summary
 The withdrawal came amid security concerns around the base where six suspects were arrested last week in connection to a suspected plot. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 The U.S. removed all its B-1 bombers from the U.K.’s RAF Fairford air base, a decision stemming from security concerns over suspected terror plots against the facility, American officials said Sunday.
 The decision represents a shift for the U.S. which has used the military base, northwest of London, as a hub for launching bomber strikes in Iran. Until their recent departure, a dozen B-1s had been stationed at the base.
 “While operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time, we can acknowledge now that all U.S. bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have redeployed to their home stations in the United States,” the Pentagon said in a statement, adding that the bombers remained ready to deliver global strike capabilities from the continental U.S. The U.K. Ministry of Defense declined to comment.
 The decision follows the arrest of six suspects in connection to a suspected attack on the base that U.S. and British official said was foiled last Sunday. U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham said there were “strong indications” that Iran played a role in the incident, which was shrouded in mystery after the U.K. released the suspects on bail but continued to investigate the situation.
 U.S. officials were aware of an Iran-linked plot to attack the bomber aircraft and kill personnel at the base, The Wall Street Journal has reported. A branch of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps had recruited U.K. nationals to carry out the plot, which involved multiple steps including a diversion in the neighborhood nearby, according to a senior U.S. official.
 In the U.K., authorities are still trying to piece together what happened, and some U.K. officials question the level of sophistication of the planned attack.

docs.title: Nifty 50 correction: why fund managers see more value in large caps now
docs.text:
Mint Money 
 Nifty 50 correction: why fund managers see more value in large caps now
 Jash Kriplani 9 min read 4 Oct 2026, 12:32 PM IST 
 Summary
 Two years of flat market returns and sharp oil-led corrections have dragged Nifty 50 valuations below historical averages. Fund managers explain why beaten-down blue chips offer a margin of safety and where to invest now. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 If you are a new investor and have stayed invested in equities over the past two years, you may have little to show for it. The Nifty 50 is down about 13% over this period and is now 14.5% below its September 2024 peak. Over the past month alone, it has fallen 6.9%. These returns are as of 1 October 2026.
 Your mutual fund statements show the same. Over the past month, large-cap funds lost 5.7% on average, mid-cap funds 6% and small-cap funds 3%. Over one and two-year periods, large-cap funds are down about 4% and 7% on average.
 After the strong returns markets delivered in the years following the covid-19 pandemic, many investors have been waiting for that run to come back. Instead, two years of flat to negative returns have left them fatigued, and the latest fall has added to the worry. Here is what fund managers say is driving the market, where they see value, and what you should do now.
 What is driving the correction 
 Fund managers cite four factors: higher global yields, expensive crude, worries about the monsoon and continued selling from foreign portfolio investors (FPIs).
 "Crude is the more important fundamental factor, along with the concern that higher global yields could signal a turn in the interest-rate cycle," said Neelesh Surana, chief investment officer at Mirae Asset Investment Managers (India). Brent crude has risen about 68% so far in 2026, now trading at $102 per barrel.
 Shailesh Bhan, CIO-equity at Nippon India Mutual Fund, said that if crude prices stay higher for longer, inflation and current account deficit challenges will be difficult to manage for India.
 India imports most of the crude oil it uses, so a higher oil bill widens the gap between what the country pays for imports and what it earns from exports. This gap has to be funded by foreign capital inflows or RBI's foreign exchange reserves, and a wider gap puts pressure on the rupee.
 The rupee, in turn, matters to foreign investors. "Foreign investors assess returns in their own currency. FCNR-B (foreign currency non-resident bank) inflows have helped stabilise the rupee to some extent, but crude moving above $100 a barrel again could raise concerns about the currency if prices remain elevated," said Harsha Upadhyaya, chief investment officer at Kotak Mahindra AMC.
 Foreign portfolio investors ( FPIs ) pulled out ₹ 35,861 crore ($3.75 billion) from Indian equities in September. Over the past two years, FPIs have net sold close to $60 billion worth of Indian equities, showed data from National Securities Depository Limited (NSDL).
 However, fund managers say India's domestic environment remains healthy. "India's high-frequency indicators are holding up, and the earnings season should be reasonably steady," said Alok Singh, CIO at Bank of India Mutual Fund.
 Drop in valuations 
 Fund managers now find the large-cap segment attractive following the fall in valuations. The Nifty 50 trades at about 17 times its one-year forward earnings, which is about 11% below its 10-year average of 18.9 times.
 "Over roughly two years, the markets have corrected by 15%, while earnings growth over the same period has compressed price-to-earnings multiples for many stocks by about 30%," said Surana.
 Upadhyaya said large caps look cheaper than smaller stocks. "Mid caps are closer to their long-term average valuations. Small caps remain at roughly a 20% premium," he said.
 Earnings growth in large caps also seems to be catching up. Large caps reported 17.6% year-on-year earnings growth in the June quarter, Upadhyaya said. Mid- and small-cap companies are growing at about 18–22% but trade at much higher valuations. "If earnings growth becomes similar, investors will need to assess whether the valuation premium is justified," he said.
 Singh said investors need to look past the headline P/E. "Even if prices remain unchanged, earnings growth can bring down the P/E multiple. Investors need to consider earnings growth alongside headline P/E multiples," he said.
 One way to do this is the price/earnings-to-growth (PEG) ratio, which divides the P/E by the expected annual growth in earnings. A company at 30 times earnings with earnings growing 30% a year has a PEG of 1.
 A company at 20 times with 10% growth has a PEG of 2. The first has the higher P/E but costs less for each unit of growth. A PEG below 1 is generally seen as reasonable value.
 Singh added that headline index valuations can also mislead. The Nifty 50 Equal Weight index, which gives every stock the same weight, has not corrected as much as the Nifty 50 .
 He pointed to IT as an example. "They may look attractive compared with historical valuations, but they are not necessarily as attractive on a multiple basis. On a PEG basis, valuations are not below one," he said.
 Sectoral outlook 
 Bhan sees IT as a potential opportunity. Large IT companies trade at about 12–13 times earnings, with earnings yields of 7–8%, he said, and "expectations are low and currency conditions are favourable."
 He expects these companies to have a role as businesses try to get value from their AI spending . "As companies and economies seek to realise value from AI investments, IT services companies will have a role, although they will need to re-engineer their business models," he said. He added that large businesses are available at valuations that are, in some cases, lower than those of smaller businesses.
 Views on financials, the other large part of the large-cap space, are more positiv

docs.title: What life insurers actually pay for
docs.text:
Mint Money What life insurers actually pay for Dhirendra Kumar (Value Research) 3 min read 4 Oct 2026, 07:00 AM IST Summary Insurance is sold as protection against death, but the industry's own numbers tell a different story Gift this article Check your portfolio This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you. Subscribe to enjoy similar stories. Subscribe now I'll give you the numbers first, and then I'll discuss them. In fiscal year 2025 (FY25), life insurers paid out ₹ 6.3 trillion in benefits, according to the insurance regulator's September 2026 consultation paper on distribution costs. Of this, death claims accounted for ₹ 0.47 trillion, or a mere 7%. Maturity benefits took 35%, surrender payouts 37%, and annuity and pension payments the remaining 20%. Read that again. Money paid to customers who gave up their policies far exceeds the money paid to families of customers who died. Surrender payments alone are five times larger than death claims. The numbers from Irdai's consultation paper deserve far more attention than the new commission rates that everyone, including me, quickly wrote about. The payoff from digging into this 120-page paper is remarkable: it contains unusually revealing data about an industry whose underlying economics are often difficult to see. These numbers should make an industry—and its regulator—uncomfortable. Life insurance exists, at least in part, to protect families from the financial consequences of a breadwinner's death. Yet death payouts are a small fraction of the industry's total benefits paid. Maturity benefits alone are nearly five times death benefits. Whatever else the industry is doing, insuring against death appears to be a relatively small part of the outcome. The bigger problem Then there is the persistency data. Overall, 61st-month persistency across the industry is just 48%, meaning fewer than half of policies remain in force after five years. By the 10th year, the proportion of policies still in force is as low as 8% for some insurance companies. That is a remarkable level of attrition. And there is a particularly interesting qualifier in the data. Online policies, bought without agent involvement, have a 61st-month persistency rate of 71%. A policyholder who bought a policy without the same degree of sales intervention is much more likely to keep it. The gap between online and agent-driven policies raises an obvious question about whether the advice being given is consistently aligned with the customer's long-term interest. The incentive structure offers part of the explanation. The paper's commission data show that first-year commissions on savings-linked policies average 25-37% of the premium. For some companies, total first-year distribution costs are as high as 60-80%. Renewal commissions on the same products range from 0-5%. The incentives are therefore heavily weighted towards acquiring a new customer rather than retaining one. It should not be surprising, then, if the industry's sales machinery is better at generating new policies than ensuring that customers stay with them. There is another loss hidden in these numbers. According to the data, even customers who surrender at around the five-year point generally do not recover the premiums they have paid. Forget returns; in many cases, they take an actual loss. The industry's defence against such criticism is that these are savings and investment products, and judging them by the standard of pure protection is unfair because customers buy them for the maturity payout, not the death benefit. But that defence gets to the heart of the problem. When customers buy products from an insurance company that function primarily as high-commission investment products with a relatively small insurance component, it raises a basic question about whether the product is doing either job particularly well. If you are holding such a policy, those surrender figures are about you, and the decision to exit is harder than the headline numbers might suggest. The premium you've already lost is gone either way. Continuing to pay for another 15 years simply to avoid acknowledging a bad purchase could turn a five-year loss into a 20-year one. A more useful comparison is forward-looking: what will the policy pay you from here? Set that against the cost of a term plan plus an index fund for the same annual outgo, and make the decision on those numbers rather than on the money already spent. None of this necessarily implies criticism of individual sellers, or any cynicism on their part. They are operating within an industry design and incentive structure that they did not create. The more important question is whether that structure produces products and advice that work in the customer's long-term interest. And the data in Irdai's paper point to a conclusion that is difficult to ignore: for someone whose primary need is life insurance, plain-term insurance remains the clearest form of protection because its purpose is straightforward—pay a benefit if the insured dies during the policy term, rather than combining insurance with a savings or investment proposition. docs.title: Why tiffin censorship threatens diversity in school classrooms
docs.text:
Lounge 
 Why tiffin censorship threatens diversity in school classrooms
 Avantika Bhuyan 5 min read 4 Oct 2026, 11:00 AM IST 
 Summary
 Rather than police tiffins, parents and schools should give children agency to decide how to share their food 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Tiffin censorship is slowly spreading through the country, turning the humble lunch box into contested ground. Parent groups petition schools to prohibit certain items, especially nonvegetarian food, from packed lunches. Their reasons range from “it smells bad”, “it goes bad quickly” to“it is not inclusive” and “it goes against our values”. Sometimes institutions enthusiastically impose restrictions to avoid “hurting popular sentiment”. A few days ago, a school in Mira-Bhayandar in Mumbai restricted food that did not align with a particular community’s festival. Unlike usual prohibitions on egg or meat, in this case the restrictions were on root vegetables and fenugreek in lunch boxes. Then government authorities intervened, warning the institution of penalties and stating that imposing dietary restrictions “violated the Right to Education Act and students’ fundamental rights”.
 The veg vs non-veg debate is not new, and now it has started impacting the shape and form of school meals. Adding to this is a new outcry on social media groups, urging parents to pack lunches that are in accordance with “Indian values”.
 It feels a little surreal that the school lunch box can cause sentiments to flare to such a degree that families are no longer just deciding what to pack for their own child’s tiffin but also dictating what others should pack. Some parents in urban areas who aspire to send their kids to foreign shores to become global citizens are not just turning their nose up at eggs and meat but simply anything unfamiliar to them. If this trend continues, lunch hour, instead of being a time of inclusivity and bonhomie, will turn into a means to segregate children based on food groups.
 Class: a space for diversity
 Isn’t school a time for exploration, when children soak in a diverse pool of cultures? They carry a little bit of themselves to the classroom and carry back a little bit of others. I remember lunch hours from my school days when most tiffins were packed with paratha-sabzi or bread in all sorts of permutations and combinations—bread jam, bread omelette, French toast, you get the drift. However, on Fridays, birthdays or other special occasions, lunch boxes would contain special treats.
 That’s when you would get a glimpse of family recipes, regional specialties, even tastes from different countries. A schoolmate from Ladakh would get cold hand-pulled noodles and during Bihu, an Assamese friend would carry boxes of pitha . A Kenyan student introduced the rest of us to his family recipe of bean stew. It was in school that I got my first taste of litti chokha, pungent chicken pickles, and “spag and meatballs”.
 The classroom has always been a space of negotiation even when it comes to food. You consume things that you are comfortable with, both culturally and in terms of your health. Tiffin does not just offer sustenance but a means to independence for the student, asserting one’s right to say no, to understand what is good for us—and in some cases, it may become a means of rebellion against prescribed norms. Even though the lunch box is packed by the parents, the kids exercise agency in how they share food in the school. The only adult intervention required is making the child and the educators aware of allergies or other non-negotiable factors—but only in the context of your own kid’s tiffin and not someone else’s.
 Take this a notch further by having discussions on diversity later at home. You will be surprised how quickly kids learn and adapt. A friend’s 10-year-old son has allergies to 20 ingredients. All he had to do was tell his classmates once and they have kept his medical needs in mind since then. They tell him at the start of lunch hour if they have a dish that could cause his allergies to flare up; they even keep a lookout for allergens, if any, in the tuck shop snacks. Isn’t this what education is about? Building empathy and learning to coexist while maintaining one’s uniqueness.
 Recently, P.C., a 14-year-old in Gurugram, started a personal project to include new items in her lunch box every week. In a matter of days, some of her classmates followed suit. “I am preparing myself for college when I will have to cook for myself. Why not start now? I want my meals to be adventurous while also being nutritious and balanced,” says the teen. She started with simple bowls of pasta, lentils or grains, tweaking them according to the cuisine she wanted to focus on that week.
 Her classmates—all of whom come from a certain degree of privilege—are turning to books, TV series and workshops for inspiration, while helping out their younger siblings as well. In the process, they have also come to understand the labour that goes into putting together a tiffin early in the morning—something they had taken for granted until now. Helping out or taking over the making of the dabba on some days is their way of acknowledging the effort. A common favourite with P.C. and her classmates is the animated series, Avatar: The Last Airbender , which features food influenced by Japanese, Tibetan and Chinese culinary cultures. P.C. tried cabbage dumplings and “did not hate it”. She made sure to inform her peers about the addition of fish sauce to the dumplings. “Some of my friends’ parents are very strict about food choices, so much so that they instruct the kids to sit a little apart if someone has brought an egg. But my classmates are alright, they do their own thing,” she adds.

 Manu Joseph: The mystery of who exactly is controlling the Tata boardroom
 Manu Joseph 4 min read 4 Oct 2026, 02:25 PM IST 
 Summary
 Perceptions exist of larger forces behind last month’s Tata boardroom coup. Whether politics really had a role to play is not as important as the optics of what’s going on. However, control of the group still can’t easily shift. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 These days, if you have a billion dollars, you can say anything and people will think it is wisdom. Jack Ma, the co-founder of Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba, used to talk a lot, and candidly, which is rare for an Asian billionaire. 
 Less than two weeks before the giant initial public offering (IPO) of his financial company, Ant, he criticized China’s financial regulators. Soon afterwards, the IPO was cancelled. Ma eventually lost control of the company. Alibaba itself came under investigation. Then, Ma disappeared for months. When he reappeared he was not so candid anymore. 
 Beijing had sent a signal to all its billionaires and the world that the Communist Party ran the show and that private enterprise was not entirely private. “This is India’s Alibaba moment,” says a top executive who works closely with Noel Tata, chairman of the Tata Trusts that have a 66% stake in Tata Sons. 
 It may not be a perfect metaphor, but I don’t think it is much of an exaggeration either. A coup has taken placed inside Tata Sons, the holding company of India’s largest business group. There are brooding whispers of political influence behind it. A brand that Indians trust appears to be under attack from a brand with which Indians have a more complicated relationship. 
 On the surface, this is what appears to be going on. Noel Tata, the relatively new chairman of the group’s charitable trusts, has lost control of Tata Sons’ board, which, led by N. Chandrasekaran, has isolated him. 
 There is division within Tata Trusts too. With this, the Trusts that have traditionally exercised control over the holding company are finding their authority challenged by the professional managers and directors, two of whom they themselves had appointed. 
 Some people may say India’s political dispensation had nothing to do with it, but I am yet to meet anyone who believes this. 
 This is what I gather is actually going on. Noel Tata sees Chandrasekaran as a part of the legacy of the group’s former patriarch, the late Ratan Tata. Ratan and Noel, half-brothers, did not have a great relationship. As long as Ratan controlled the group, Noel was eclipsed. 
 On the other hand, Chandrasekaran thrived. Last fiscal year, he drew over ₹ 158 crore in annual compensation. After the demise of Ratan Tata, Noel took over the Trusts, and he questioned the business record under Chandrasekaran. Last year, Air India lost over ₹ 22,000 crore and Tata Digital lost nearly ₹ 5,000 crore. 
 In August, it seemed that Chandrasekaran felt he had no cards against the new chairman of Tata Trusts, and since Noel Tata did not want him given a third term in his role, he decided to leave when his current term ended in February 2027. But something happened in the weeks after that. On 17 September, everyone on the board, except Noel Tata, asked Chandrasekaran to stay on. 
 People tell me that in the vacuum of stature that Rata Tata’s departure created, powerful people saw an opportunity to take control of a vast business empire. A few days ago, Chandrasekaran reportedly called for a new university with a curriculum that blended “Hindu shastras ” with artificial intelligence. Even though I do not know what he is talking about, this is the sort of stuff that’s music to the ears of India’s ruling party. 
 In contrast to this, the old-world charm and anglicized refinement of the Tata family may suggest that they might be culturally distant from India’s ruling elite. But, an insider tells me, many rich Parsis are right-wing. And not just today. A prominent Parsi doyen funded the right long before it achieved power. “So that’s not the issue here,” says the insider. 
 Whether politics had a role in the Tata coup is not as important as perceptions among some observers of political games being played in the background and of the Tata Group being yet another Indian institution whose independence is no longer guaranteed. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi recently suggested that Tata Consultancy Services was pressured into doing something shady for the Election Commission of India’s software systems. 
 The men on both sides of the Tata dispute claim high principles as the reason behind their actions. For instance, transparency is at the heart of one of the issues the group is split over. Tata Sons, which owns stakes in many companies whose shares are publicly traded, is not listed. All Tata patriarchs wanted it that way. Including Ratan Tata. 
 Chandrasekaran is also thought to have held this view until recently. The Reserve Bank of India wants a financial company of such significance to go public so that it meets higher norms of disclosure on its business affairs. 
 But the Tatas never wanted it, chiefly because a listed company is under pressure to meet short-term financial objectives, while they wanted Tata Sons to think long term without being flustered by monetary upheavals. They also wanted to keep dividends flowing for charity. Noel Tata has repeated this. 
 Tata’s stated reasons for not listing are not persuasive. Mark Zuckerberg, who controls Meta via shares with outsized voting power, makes costly long-term bets, like he did on the metaverse and is doing on AI, even if the market punishes Meta’s stock for these. 
 With a 66% stake in Tata Sons, the Trusts needn’t lose control of it once a quarter of its equity floats. The equity arithmetic suggests the company could still choose to make long-term bets and yield payouts for charity. Yet, for some reason, Noel
